title: docc diff output
description: What docc diff <base> <head> --format json prints: one object on one line. Each side is compiled from its own revision as docc compile --rev does (the reader's pages: hidden documents are left out), and the blocks of a document are lined up across the two.

base.description: The commit of base (its tree when base is a tree, such as the empty tree).

files.description: Without --path: every document Git reports changed between the two, in Git's order. With --path: that document only (empty when neither side has it).

status.description: Added, modified, deleted, renamed; = only with --path, for a document that did not change.

path.description: Relative to src, in head (for D in base).

oldPath.description: R only: the path in base.

title.description: The title of the page in head, else in base; empty when neither side compiles.

blocks.description: The properties, then the blocks of the page, lined up. Without --path only add, rm and ch in document order; with --path every block, same included: new blocks keep their order and a removed block stands before the next block that followed it, so the ops read as two aligned columns. op compares the source text s (the HTML of the footnotes block, which has none); h may differ in a same block when a link or include target changed.

broken.description: A side of the file is in a revision that does not compile (errors of groups 1xx-2xx or a broken docc.json): blocks is empty.

block.description: A block as docc compile prints it; a property (a one-line field of the list) has k and sec null.

p.description: JSON Pointer of the value in the source of that side; empty for the footnotes.

k.description: A property: the field name as a heading.
